feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with strong evidence of scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Strong credibility through concrete tools, platforms, and responsibilities across strategy, CMS, analytics, and multimedia.  
- Executive-ready positioning in the header: focused, relevant, and aligned to mission-driven/public-sector communications work.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap heavily and could be consolidated for a cleaner structure.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, especially in recent roles (e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, campaign results).  
- Fix writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent punctuation in lists (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other lists without the serial comma); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and fix style: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience.”
- Add sharper positioning tied to recent roles: emphasize digital transformation, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, and mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) in favor of outcomes and leadership scope.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web modernization, cross-channel communications, and content operations for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in Drupal platforms, editorial workflow design, analytics, and stakeholder coordination, with a strong track record of translating complex policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions; keep the intro broader unless targeting advocacy-specific roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, outcome-oriented language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Standardize phrasing for parallel structure; avoid mixing functions, tools, and soft skills in one list.
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Cross-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Advocacy & policy communications • Stakeholder leadership • Multimedia & live event production
- Use “cross-channel communications” instead of “multi-channel communication” for consistency with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates the header and Soft Skills section.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and Topline Skills/Technical sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and avoid repeating project details already covered in Recent Projects.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations into one impact-focused line: “Built cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet outcome-oriented: mention scale, speed, usability, or stakeholder adoption if available. E.g., “Developed Drupal campaign microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits that improved launch speed and content reuse.”
- Keep the AI search bullet, but add a measurable or strategic result if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy and structured content workflows to improve policy-content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for that section.
- “Governance” and “analytics” also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new or more advanced here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets by impact: website migration, analytics infrastructure, video studio, governance/operations; put routine channel oversight last or trim it.
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add launch timing, performance gains, production savings, reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, or engagement growth.
- Suggested phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video/programming language may duplicate older NACo roles and recent projects; emphasize building the in-house studio as the leadership-level achievement.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact distinct from the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy distribution.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & message architecture
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable outcomes for experience bullets rather than this skills list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo roles; “membership” adds useful specificity.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and implementation strengths rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first, and consider removing jQuery.
- If SharePoint/Power Pages matter for target jobs, group them as secondary: “Additional platforms: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages.”
- Use “enterprise CMS modernization” instead of “CMS modernization” to better match recent leadership scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it in one place unless wording is differentiated.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it largely duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” technical section and misses a chance to signal strategic value. For a topline skills area, make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic items with higher-value phrasing: “Analytics infrastructure and dashboarding” instead of listing tools plus “leadership reporting”
- Tighten strategic skills to: “KPI framework design • Executive reporting • SEO and performance optimization”
- If space allows, order by seniority/value: strategy first, then platforms, e.g. “KPI framework design • Executive reporting • Analytics infrastructure • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrase.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, selective, and tied to the strongest recent/most credible capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, higher-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Drop “video production and editing” if you want a more leadership-level tone; “broadcast-quality video production” implies editing without sounding junior.
- Consider adding one stronger differentiator if accurate: “Recurring advocacy video programming” or “Virtual event production workflows.”
- Keep to 4 items max; this section should signal capability, not restate duties.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use either this section or that phrase there, not both.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already supported by the Director of Digital Media entry, so avoid expanding this into task-level detail here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal level/relevance, with Drupal first given the recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency cues tied to recency: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint/Power Pages (working knowledge) • GitHub Pages**
- Keep only platforms here; avoid adding CMS modernization or AI/search language since those already appear elsewhere.
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially relevant to target roles; it reads lighter than the enterprise platforms above.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- If both sections stay, make Topline Skills broader and keep this one strictly as a concise tools list with proficiency/context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Deployment/automation: GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add a brief qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “for Drupal-based public-facing sites, analytics tagging, and lightweight workflow automation.”
- Order by relevance to recent roles: JavaScript/APIs/GTM first; jQuery later if still actively used.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” and “Cloudflare Workers” are useful differentiators; keep those here and trim repeated basics elsewhere if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize systems ownership, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Group by function for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue tracking: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers tied to recent work: “used to build editorial workflows, cross-team planning systems, approvals, and lightweight automations.”
- Keep only the strongest/recently used tools; consider dropping older/general collaboration apps if they weren’t central to 2022–present roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them verbatim without added context.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless tied to operational use; they can dilute stronger automation tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and misses the scale/context already shown in recent NACo roles. Tighten it and, if possible, signal enterprise email/association use rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, and member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, put it first and consider dropping the least relevant/oldest tool to keep the list sharper.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- “Engagement” may feel vague alongside “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; “Member Engagement” or “Email Marketing” is clearer.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than achievement. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and content output, with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social, and video.”
- Split the rest into 2 concise outcome-focused bullets, e.g.:
- “Supported a major website refresh, contributing content, coordination, and publishing improvements for NACo’s public-facing web presence.”
- “Produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if possible: number of livestreams/videos, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version framed as launching/building the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is echoed in later NACo entries; use lighter wording here to avoid repetition.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work at NACo. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation role, with the podcast launch as the clearest standout achievement.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the digital work more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications.”
- Elevate the strongest accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing if later NACo roles already cover multimedia extensively; keep this focused on podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Don’t overstate leadership here since stronger management and platform ownership appear in later, more senior roles.
